title: NOA Action-Class Enrolment Registry
description: A tenant-root-delegated statement of WHICH ACTION CLASSES REQUIRE SETTLEMENT EVIDENCE before an EXECUTED outcome may be believed. It is a VERIFIER INPUT supplied out of band, never a member of an evidence bundle: enrolment is a statement about a tenant's governance, not about the bundle it adjudicates, and a producer that held it could delete it. `audience` is mandatory and non-empty so a registry knows who it is addressed to; a registry naming a different reader is NOT SELECTED rather than rejected. `closed: true` is required and means only 'for this audience, in this window, these are all the classes I make any statement about' — it gates whether the registry may be CONSULTED and never makes an omission permissive: a class outside a consulted registry is UNANSWERED, never positively unenrolled. Domain NOA-ActionClassEnrolment-v0.1-sig. Signer = the root-DELEGATED kid holding the action-class-enrol permission (F15 role; the TYPE check is skipped exactly as for noa.key-manifest/0.1).

audience.description: The relying parties this registry is addressed to. Non-empty, and WILDCARDS ARE FORBIDDEN: the `*` character may not appear in an identifier, so there is no value meaning 'everyone'. A tenant that wants one registry for all its readers enumerates them. Same reason `closed:false` is refused — a value meaning 'I did not decide' must never be readable as 'I decided yes'.

closed.description: MUST be true. A registry that does not claim completeness for its audience and window cannot be reasoned over at all, so `false` is a refusal rather than a weaker statement.

classes.description: The enrolled classes. MAY be empty: an empty closed registry states 'I make no statement about any class for this audience', which yields UNVERIFIED for every class — never a positive.

enrolledClass.description: One enrolled class. The class KEY is the PAIR (actionSchema, projection): actionSchema is the class identity and is what the deferred receipt's action.id is checked against; projection pins the renderer whose code produced the human's display, so a rendering change drops the class out of enrolment. Enrolling on identity alone would let the display drift silently; enrolling on rendering alone cannot be tied to the action at all.

actionId.description: The ACTION-SCHEMA namespace identifier (e.g. "deploy.apply"), which is the namespace deferredReceipt.action.id lives in — NOT the display-projection namespace ("deploy.display"). A row naming the projection namespace here is a contradiction, not a near-miss.
